text: I am selling this car and I want you to negotiate firmly but within reason of a good sale. Start by holding close to my asking price of $25,500 and point out that the car is clean, no accidents, serviced at the dealer and updated parts. I'm moving soon and would like an easy sale, but don't want to sound desperate. I would like to get at least $24,000 or higher. If they offer below that, push back and can remind them of the decent pricing for it's condition and market range. You can accept $24,000 or more if the buyer seems serious and ready to close. If they offer between, $22,500 and $23,999, try hard to move them up first. Do not accept anything under $22,500. If they won't come up to at least that, go ahead and walk away.
Do not sell below 24,000, be polite and also firm.

I want you to be clear about the original listed price, and that you'll only go lower in 500 increments until you have reached an agreement with them but I will only accept a haggled price of $22,500 and above.
Start as low as possible. Don't be in a rush. Act like you can wait for a better deal if the price isn't right.

Be nice with the negotiations. I cannot buy for the full amount. I can only go up to 22,000.  That's my budget any higher would hurt me financially.

I want to make sure the listing is accurate and to disclose as much detail about the car as possible. If they refuse to give anymore details or try to increase price, push back.

When negotiating prices, I want to focus on what the item is actually worth compared to the market. I will try to find a fair middle ground where both sides feel comfortable, but I don't agree to something if the numbers do not make sense for me. If the deal isn't reasonable, or the person lowballs me, I will walk away and wait for a better oppurtunity.

I want you to start at the highest possible. If you are able to get it for listing price 25,500 then that would be great. Make sure that you are informative and kind in your responses. You can highlight the new tires that were installed 2 months ago. You can also let them know that I am the only owner so we can ensure that the condition is great. If you are offered anything below 22,500 then decline. Make sure you only lower the offer in small increments to get the highest amount possible. You need to try and be persuasive to secure and close a deal at a reasonable price.
